observation: call_routine's ROM0/HOME-target path (address < 0x4000) sets PC directly and relies on returning to the injected 0x3FFF sentinel with no Bankswitch indirection. In this build 0x3FFF is ROM padding ($FF = RST 38), so the callee's own final ret unwinds into RST 38 -> $0038 and runs whatever unrelated real game code happens to be mapped there, instead of returning to the caller. The ROMX-target path is unaffected: Bankswitch's own .Return label is a real, always-mapped ROM0 address reached before the final ret pops 0x3FFF. Every existing call_routine usage in this suite targets a ROMX label, so this path was apparently never exercised - found 2026-08-27 porting _Divide (engine/math/multiply_divide.asm), where it silently returned a plausible-looking wrong result (no crash, no timeout, a repeating garbage pattern from an unrelated background call).
decision_needed: Either fix call_routine to route ROM0/HOME targets through Bankswitch too (bank=0 is safe: the fixed $0000-$3FFF region is unaffected by the bank-select write, so this gives both paths the same safe .Return hop) or explicitly document that call_routine must not be trusted for a ROM0/HOME target and callers should hook a label inside the routine instead of relying on its return.
test_boundary: Any call_routine(label) where label resolves to an address below $4000 is affected. All current test-suite usages (CriticalHitTest, ApplySingleBadgeStatBoost, AISelectSendOut, ProcPreloadAssignedWildArea, SaveGameData, LoadMainData) target ROMX and are unaffected.

observation: call_routine hijacks PC from wherever the CPU happens to be parked when the previous helper stopped ticking, and boot_fight2 stops the instant its MainInBattleLoop hook fires. That resume point is an accident of cycle timing, not a defined state, so any engine change that shifts when the battle loop is reached moves it. Measured 2026-09-01 with an AISelectSendOut change that makes the OPENING send-out skip the scored candidate scan (strictly less work, and behaviourally a no-op for this fixture): boot_fight2(seed=1) ended at frame 1583, PC=$211E, SP=$DFDB, bank $01 before the change and frame 1566, PC=$1435, SP=$DFDD, bank $02 after it. Battle state was byte-identical either way (same party species, same lead slot 0, same species/level/HP), zero symbols changed bank, and no RST 38 occurred during boot. But the three test_laundry_scope tests, which all call_routine immediately after boot_fight2, went from passing to a runaway RST 38 with SP walking down into VRAM ($91D7) - because PC was overwritten mid-routine in bank $02 instead of at the benign spot the old timing happened to produce. The ROM is not at fault; the fixture's implicit assumption is. ROOT CAUSE FOUND: the two resume points were VBlank.ok+$22 (before) and LoadFrontSpriteByMonIndex+$2 (after). call_routine can safely hijack PC out of the VBlank handler - the code it interrupted is itself at a clean instruction boundary waiting for the frame, and the handler saves and restores what it touches - but NOT out of ordinary main-loop code caught mid-routine with a live stack frame and a ROM bank it switched to itself. PyBoy's tick() returns at a frame boundary, which usually but not always lands in VBlank, so every existing usage silently depended on that coincidence.
decision_needed: PARTIAL FIX APPLIED, review completed 2026-09-02. boot_fight2 parks at the defined VBlank boundary. call_routine and probe_routine_until now both document that injected routines must not wait for VBlank/a frame or require interrupts. Global non-ticking enforcement was prototyped and rejected: it correctly exposed 29 callers outside that narrow boundary, but several intentionally operate from other controlled states and boot_to_lobby cannot simply tick to VBlank. Naively parking after lobby readiness advanced the live flow into EnemySendOutFirstMon and failed the lobby smoke test. General enforcement therefore remains unresolved and needs either a non-advancing, interrupt-safe trampoline/context mechanism or helper-specific entry contracts. Do not add implicit ticking inside either hijack helper.
test_boundary: Verified: full smoke went from 43 errors (17 real once an unrelated missing ROM was rebuilt) to 152/154, the two remaining being the pre-existing test_follower_yellow_runtime CGB-classification and test_lobby_pose_layout failures that already failed at clean HEAD. make integration clean, make ai_scenarios 56/56.
